findings.description: Collision removal deletes production modules as well as collected test modules. For example, fixture tests/helpers.py reserves helpers.py, so an agent-added src/pkg/helpers.py is deleted. An overlay __init__.py similarly reserves every newly added package initializer.
findings.failure_mode: A correct solution loses required source files before any grading command runs, causing import failures or changed package behavior and a false failing grade.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict removal to modules that actually collide under pytest collection and import rules. Exclude package initializers and ordinary source/helper modules from basename-based deletion.

findings.description: Directory overlays contribute no filenames to reserved: owned explicitly excludes directories, and owned_dirs is used only to exempt paths from deletion.
findings.failure_mode: With hidden tests supplied through a directory overlay, an agent-added test with the same basename remains. Package-less pytest collection still aborts with an import-file-mismatch error, defeating the collision fix and falsely failing the solution.
findings.suggested_fix: Walk directory overlay contents when building the reserved test-module set, while preserving their destination paths as owned.

findings.description: The jq fallback operator treats false and null as absent. Consequently, run_usd_by_type: false and entries such as build: false or build: null silently select the fallback cap, despite the documented requirement to reject present malformed values.
findings.failure_mode: A malformed spending configuration launches trials under an unintended cap instead of returning the promised usage error.
findings.suggested_fix: Use explicit key-presence checks to distinguish missing settings from present values, then validate the map and each present entry before applying fallbacks.

findings.description: The reserved-basename set is far wider than the pytest 'import file mismatch' it targets, and the removal walk covers the whole tree, not just package-less test directories. Three concrete over-reaches: (a) every .py under a fixture tests/ or test/ directory is reserved, including non-collected support modules (helpers.py, utils.py, fixtures.py); the 1.2.11 comment itself documents that hidden suites do `from helpers import …`, so helpers.py is reserved in exactly the suites this rule runs on. (b) Overlay-derived names are not filtered: `reserved = {d.rsplit('/',1)[-1] for d in owned if d.endswith('.py')}` keeps `__init__.py` if any overlay ships one, while the fixture scan explicitly excludes it. (c) Matches are deleted anywhere in the tree (src/, app/, new packages), and even inside proper packages where pytest's rootdir-based naming would never collide. An agent that adds `src/<pkg>/helpers.py` or `utils.py` (very common in feature-build tasks) while the fixture or overlay has `tests/helpers.py` loses that module before test_command runs.
findings.failure_mode: ImportError / ModuleNotFoundError in the hidden suite or in the agent's own code paths; a correct solution is graded as failing (hidden_tests 0/N), with only a telemetry count (colliding_tests_removed) hinting at the cause. Silent corruption of the graded tree, biased against arms that add more source modules.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict `reserved` to modules pytest actually collects by basename (test_*.py, *_test.py per the fixture's python_files setting) and drop `__init__.py`/`conftest.py` from the overlay-derived set too. Restrict deletion to candidates pytest would import as top-level modules: files whose directory (and ancestors up to rootdir) has no `__init__.py`, and preferably only under tests/ or test/ components. Never remove a file that is imported by another retained module (or at minimum never remove non-test_* modules). Add an AG test where the agent adds src/pkg/helpers.py alongside a fixture tests/helpers.py and assert it survives.

findings.description: required_until = now + 2 × Σ watchdog_s / concurrency over the WHOLE plan. watchdog_s is already 2× the phase-sum (per the RAB-1 comments: 140 min → 16800 s), so the horizon is ~4× summed phase time. It also counts a0_bare trials (which the same function says never use codex) and, on --resume, every already-rowed trial. For the suite v2 full batch (8 arms × 16 tasks × 3 trials ≈ 384 trials, ~15000 s watchdog each, concurrency 3) that is ≈ 44 days; even one arm on the full suite is ≈ 5–6 days. No OAuth access token issued by `codex login` lives that long, and the refusal message tells the operator to run `codex login`, which cannot change the token lifetime. There is no override flag.
findings.failure_mode: Every non-smoke full-suite batch, and any --resume of a large batch late in its life (even with only a handful of trials left), exits with REFUSED.txt and never launches. --dry-run (used to produce MANIFEST/plan for pre-registration) is refused too. The runner becomes unusable for its primary purpose until the formula is changed.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the horizon over remaining, codex-using trials only (plan entries without a row on --resume; exclude arms where uses_codex is false), and use the realistic expected duration (phase_sum or est from history), not 2× an already-doubled watchdog. Alternatively keep the watchdog sum but cap the comparison to the token's actual lifetime semantics (e.g. refuse only when exp is before now + the next ~concurrency × watchdog, since later runs can be refused per-trial), and add a documented --skip-codex-preflight / warn-only mode. Record required_until in the manifest either way.

findings.description: Directory overlays (owned_dirs) contribute no basenames to `reserved`: only file overlays are scanned (`for d in owned if d.endswith('.py')`). A hidden suite overlaid as a directory (e.g. tests/hidden/ → tree) still collides with an agent file of the same basename in another package-less directory.
findings.failure_mode: pytest aborts collection with 'import file mismatch' for suites whose hidden tests ship as a directory overlay; the 1.2.11 fix does not apply and a correct solution grades as failing, while grade.json reports colliding_tests_removed = 0.
findings.suggested_fix: os.walk each directory overlay source and add its collected test-module basenames to `reserved` (with the same test_*.py restriction suggested in DISS-001).

findings.description: The jq filter uses `//` twice: `.caps.run_usd_by_type // null` and `(.[$k] // "")`. In jq, `false` and `null` are both swallowed by `//`, so `run_usd_by_type: false` or `build: null`/`build: false` silently fall through to the single-cap chain, contradicting the comment 'A present but malformed per-kind entry is refused, never skipped' and the header's usage-error promise.
findings.failure_mode: A typo'd or templated-out suite value (false/null) yields a different per-run cap than the operator intended, without any diagnostic; MANIFEST records the fallback as the effective cap.
findings.suggested_fix: Test presence with `has($k)` and type explicitly: `if has($k) then (.[$k] | if type == "number" or type == "string" then tostring else "!" end) else "" end`, and treat a non-object (including false) as "!" via `if type == "object"` on the raw value rather than after `// null`.

findings.description: Only tokens.refresh_token is rewritten; last_refresh is copied verbatim. The codex CLI decides to refresh proactively based on last_refresh age (not only on a 401), so a per-run copy whose last_refresh is older than the CLI's refresh interval will attempt a refresh with the placeholder, fail, and may report the run as logged out even though the access token the pre-flight validated is still good. This is a KF-048 recurrence-3 shape the preflight cannot catch because it only reads exp.
findings.failure_mode: Rows degrade (no OpenAI voice) despite a passing codex preflight, with the failure attributed to the container rather than to the stale last_refresh field.
findings.suggested_fix: Set data["last_refresh"] to the current UTC timestamp in the copy (or verify against the pinned codex CLI version that proactive refresh keys off access-token exp rather than last_refresh, and document that), and add a pipeline-run test asserting the copied last_refresh is fresh.
